### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **6** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-i18n`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, `@objectstack/service-storage`, `@objectstack/types`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-storage/src/metadata-store.ts`, `packages/types/src/server-fault-log.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bbb975771781c0d75e0a367b956661c3745c2788`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-storage/src/metadata-store.ts`, `packages/types/src/server-fault-log.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **45** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bbb975771781c0d75e0a367b956661c3745c2788` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `75904b8c4d17dfb2651e5a8aa4fe53fcdffd1834` — the merge of head `3c34255a8b1a204d50e39610d1bd12c5919d5aaa` into base `bbb975771781c0d75e0a367b956661c3745c2788`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 75904b8c4d17dfb2651e5a8aa4fe53fcdffd1834 && git checkout 75904b8c4d17dfb2651e5a8aa4fe53fcdffd1834
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bbb975771781c0d75e0a367b956661c3745c2788 3c34255a8b1a204d50e39610d1bd12c5919d5aaa && git checkout -B drift-repro bbb975771781c0d75e0a367b956661c3745c2788 && git merge --no-ff 3c34255a8b1a204d50e39610d1bd12c5919d5aaa

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bbb975771781c0d75e0a367b956661c3745c2788
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bbb975771781c0d75e0a367b956661c3745c2788` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3e9d931731fe31bf6b1bc3bbf029e617b2b764ff`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #23174 (body and all ten comments), PR #23346 (body, the one bot comment, the 17-file list, the net diff `origin/main...3e9d93173` over merge base `cc14657ed`), the 47 check-runs on the head, and `origin/main` at `3490bf5fa` for context (`@objectstack/types`' `response-envelope.ts`, `server-fault-log.ts`, `thrown-http-error.ts`, `error-leak.ts`; `packages/rest/src/error-response.ts`; the runtime dispatcher's `errorResponseBase`, `errorFromThrown`, `domains/i18n.ts`, `domains/share-links.ts`, `dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts`; `plugin-sharing`'s `share-link-service.ts`; `plugin-security`'s `errors.ts`; `plugin-hono-server`'s `adapter.ts`; `core`'s `kernel.ts`; `cli`'s `serve.ts`; `spec`'s `contract.zod.ts`; ADR-0112; ADR-0076 OQ#9; `.changeset/config.json`; `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs`). `origin/main` is 11 commits past the merge base and touches none of the 17 files (measured: `git diff --stat cc14657ed origin/main -- the 17 paths` is empty).

**Check-runs on the head:** 47, all `completed`. The five required contexts are `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (and its six shards), `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. Eight are `skipped` by path filter or opt-in (Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Regression Gate shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Build Docs, Temporal Conformance, Packed-tarball smoke, and one each of the duplicate Auto Label / Check PR Size runs). Nothing is `in_progress`. No governed path in the file list.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The widening is exactly the one export triage named, and minimal — right.** `sendServerFault(res, status, code: ErrorCode, message, thrown: unknown, request?: ServerFaultRequest)` is the only new `export` in the diff. It reaches the package index through the existing `export * from './response-envelope.js'` (`packages/types/src/index.ts:31`), so no index edit was needed and none was made. `writeErrorEnvelope` is a plain `function` declaration with no `export` keyword: module-private, and a non-exported declaration is never emitted into `dist/index.d.ts`, so it is absent from the published declarations. `ServerFaultRequest` was already public (`server-fault-log.ts`, re-exported at index line 41), so the signature introduces no second new surface. `sendError`'s signature is byte-identical; only its body now delegates the write.

2. **`request?: ServerFaultRequest` has to be there — right.** Its one caller is `sendRawByteRouteFailure` (`storage-routes.ts:246`), which passes `route`, the mounted pattern `{ method, path }` that PR #23172 already keyed the line by; the writer forwards it to `logServerFault` as the log's `where` and as the #14656 dedupe key. The type may carry three strings (`method`, `path`, `requestId`); the writer never calls `describeFaultRequest`, so no raw request object is read, and no converted arm passes a request at all. The guard that `path` is a pattern and never a URL is the writer's doc plus the storage pins (token absent from every console argument), not the type — acceptable, and it is the same guard the field had on `logServerFault` before this PR.

3. **Disclosure on the converted arms — storage, settings, i18n right; share-link wrong (the FAIL item, ③ f2).** On storage's 8 catch-alls plus the raw-byte arm, settings' 4 `refuse` tails and i18n's 3 arms, `code` is a literal, `message` is the route's literal text, `thrown` goes only to `logServerFault`, no `extra` is passed, and `writeErrorEnvelope(res, status, code, message)` with `extra` undefined writes exactly `{ success: false, error: { code, message } }` — so `details`, `userMessage`, `declaredCode` and `httpStatus` have no path from the caught error, and no header is written on the fault path (the share-link public routes' `Cache-Control` / `Vary` are constants). The share-link undeclared-status branch, however, writes `err?.code ?? 'INTERNAL'` into `error.code`: the caught error's own `code` string goes on the wire, unvalidated. Named wrong; reach in ③.

4. **The log line names the mounted pattern and never the request URL — right.** `serverFaultLogMessage` prints `[5xx] STATUS METHOD PATH — text` from `request.path` as passed; the converted arms pass no `request`, so the line carries no path; the raw-byte arm passes the pattern. Pinned on both storage token routes (line contains `PUT /api/v1/storage/_local/raw/:token`, token absent from all console arguments) and on the share-link token routes (token absent).

5. **Authored arms, triage's limit — every classification right; no arm wrongly placed either way.** Kept on `sendError`: storage `:592` and `:682` (brand-guarded `isAuthzStoreUnavailableError` relays, declared `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`), `:1482 :1534 :1552 :1597` (`501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, literal text), `:1254` (`409 CHUNK_NOT_RECORDED`, authored, a 4xx anyway); settings `:145` (`relayAuthzStoreOutage`, brand-guarded) and `:344` (`SETTINGS_CRYPTO_UNAVAILABLE`: `err.message` is the class's own prescription, with `details { namespace, key }`, which the console renders); share-link's declared-status half, which `makeError` (`share-link-service.ts:342`, always status + code), `PermissionDeniedError` (status 403) and `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` (status 503) all take. Switched: exactly the arms whose message was `err?.message ?? fallback` — the catch-all shape — storage 8 (`:979 :1035 :1134 :1290 :1393 :1452 :1491 :1540`) plus the raw-byte 500 arm, settings `:245 :266 :348 :381`, i18n `:178 :193 :228`, share-link `:285`'s undeclared half. The census at the merge base reproduces the PR's table; no other 5xx `sendError` site in the four files passes caught text.

6. **One line per fault — right, with one unmeasured corner.** The writer calls `logServerFault` once and a write that does not log, so a converted arm logs one line; the raw-byte arm goes from two (`logServerFault` then `sendError`'s own) to one, and the CONTROL case in `server-fault-log.test.ts` measures the replaced composition at two. No converted arm logs elsewhere, so none logs two. Zero lines is possible only through #14656's quiet branch, which the share-link `err?.code` pass-through can reach (③ f2); every other converted arm passes a literal `INTERNAL` / `INTERNAL_ERROR` at 500, which never quiets.

7. **#14656 capability-absence quieting unchanged for both writers — right.** `isDeclaredCapabilityAbsence` reads `input.status` and `input.code` only; `sendServerFault` passes `{ status, code, error, message, request }`, the same `code` `sendError` passes, so the predicate sees the same envelope at both exits. The branded outage relays (503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, kept on `sendError`) keep the quieting they had.

8. **`check:route-envelope`'s SHARED_BUILDER pin (2 / 1 / 1) holds — right.** `sendOk` has one `res.status().json`, `writeErrorEnvelope` the other, `sendError` none now. `Lint & Repo Gates` is green on the head.

9. **Fixture re-pins — right.** `storage-routes.metadata-outage.test.ts` (10 sites), `chunk-part-record-concurrency.test.ts` (1), `settings-routes.authz-outage-relay.test.ts` §3 (1): each now asserts the generic text in the body, the absence of the sentence from the body, and the sentence in a `[5xx]` line — the same distinguishing claim, on the side the rule puts it.

10. **`metadata-store.ts` docblock (patch round) — right.** Against `storage-routes.ts` on this head every catch-all hands the caught error to `sendServerFault`, and the `Cause:` tail is built in `metadata-store.ts`; the new sentence is true.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/types`: `minor` — right.** One added export; nothing removed, renamed or narrowed; `sendError`'s published signature and wire behaviour are unchanged.
- **`@objectstack/service-storage`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, `@objectstack/service-i18n`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`: `patch` — right.** What changes is the `message` text of a declared 500 from caught text to the route's generic text; `status` and `code` are unchanged; no published TypeScript shape moves. The storage outage sentence that moves to the log is named in the changeset, and the PR measured no consumer of it (objectui `72594f29`).
- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)` — right.** `yes` with `minor` meets the floor; the arm is the closed pair's `(widening)`; no narrowing, so no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. The changeset body carries no angle bracket and no model identifier.
- **`packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts` needs no changeset entry — right.** The module is not exported from `packages/runtime/src/index.ts`, tsup's entry is `src/index.ts` alone, and its only importer outside the gate script is `error-envelope.conformance.test.ts`; nothing from it reaches `@objectstack/runtime`'s `dist`. `Check Changeset` is green. All five bumped packages and runtime sit in the one `fixed` group, so versions move in lockstep regardless.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Deviations in `6156490092`:**
- d1, the runtime ledger file outside the claim (two `compiler-narrowed` rows): accepted — gate-required and non-shipping, measured above. One note folded into f2: the new `sendServerFault` row's `why` repeats `sendError`'s claim that an unregistered spelling "fails the build before it reaches the fault log or the envelope". By the gate's definition the verdict is about the helper's parameter, so the row stands; but the claim is false at a caller whose `err` is typed `any`, where `err?.code ?? 'INTERNAL'` is `any` and assignable to `ErrorCode` — which is exactly the share-link arm.
- d2, fixtures re-pinned to the log side: accepted (①9).
- d3, first push refused by the pre-push trailer hook and amended before anything was published: accepted, REPORTING only.
- d4, not merged with `origin/main`: accepted — none of the 17 files moved on `main` (measured above); the queue validates the merged generation.
- d5, `check:type-check-debt`'s unlocked closure build killed 137 and partial dist rebuilt: accepted — `TypeScript Type Check` is green on the head.
- d6, `metadata-store.ts` docblock left stale: closed by the patch round (①10).

**Deviation in `6156816704`:** the PR body edited once by the seat's order: accepted.

**`out_of_scope_findings`:**

- **f1 (first report) — `StorageMetadataStoreError` docblock:** closed by the patch round; the new text is accurate on this head.

- **f2 — the share-link catch-all keeps `err?.code ?? 'INTERNAL'`: answered, and it BLOCKS this PR.** Reach, traced on `origin/main`:
  - Every service-authored throw declares a status, so it takes the `sendError` half: `makeError` (`share-link-service.ts:342-346`) sets `status` and `code` together; `PermissionDeniedError` declares `status = 403` (`plugin-security/src/errors.ts:42-44`); `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` declares 503. So the undeclared-status half's realistic population is engine and driver throws: `createLink` re-throws `readRecord`'s engine throw as it came (`share-link-service.ts:590-621`); `listLinks`, `revokeLink`, `resolveToken`, and the routes' own `engine.find` calls (the probe row, the record read, the messages read) throw whatever the driver throws. Node system errors carry `code: 'ECONNREFUSED'` / `'ENOENT'`, Postgres `'42P01'`, SQLite `'SQLITE_ERROR'`, MySQL `'ER_NO_SUCH_TABLE'` — string `.code`, no `.status`.
  - That is the exact population the platform already ruled on: `thrown-http-error.ts` names "a driver errno (`SQLITE_ERROR`, `42P01`)" as "measured on the wire at three of this repo's doors" and the reason `demotedDeclaredCode` withholds the spelling on an UNDECLARED 5xx (#12509, ruled 2026-08-27, option D) — "the spelling names the backend, which is one of the two disclosures the 5xx message withhold exists to prevent". ADR-0112's 2026-08-17 amendment (#9106, #9232) makes `error.code` closed at EVERY door. The dispatcher twin of these same five routes (`runtime/src/domains/share-links.ts:473`, `deps.errorFromThrown`) therefore withholds it; this door, after this PR, still writes it raw into `error.code` on a 500.
  - It is also a contract violation on the wire: `ApiErrorSchema.code` is the closed `ErrorCode` (`spec/src/api/contract.zod.ts:29`, "an unregistered code fails parse"), so a `500 { code: '42P01' }` body fails `BaseResponseSchema`. The PR's own pin asserts that parse, but drives only `new Error(FAULT)` with no `code`, so the channel is unmeasured by the PR's evidence — the dev's "read-only inference, unmeasured" is right about the measurement and wrong about the conclusion: the reach is established by the repo's own records above.
  - Corollary: a caught `code` of `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` or `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` with no status trips #14656's quiet branch at the writer — `warn`, no stack, and with no `request` key, every time — so this arm can also cost the fault its `error` line.
  - Why it is this PR's and not a card: the card is a security disclosure card about a caught error's text reaching the caller on exactly these catch-all arms; the PR rewrites this line and converts it half-way — `message` closed, `code` open — in a diff whose point is that the thrown value "has no path into the body". Triage's limit ("withholds only text that came from a caught error") covers a caught error's `code`.
  - Required to pass: in the undeclared-status branch, write no caught spelling to `error.code` unless it is a vocabulary member — either the literal `'INTERNAL'`, or `resolveThrownHttpError(err).code` (`@objectstack/types`), which keeps a registered spelling and puts nothing demoted on the wire for an undeclared 5xx; and one pin, on at least one token route, driving a throw with `code: '42P01'` and no status, asserting `error.code` is `'INTERNAL'` (or a registered code), that `BaseResponseSchema` parses the body, and that `42P01` appears nowhere in the body. The `sendError` half (declared status) may keep `err?.code`: a producer that declares its 5xx is the `'declared'` limb, where the code survives by the same ruling.

- **f3 — the runtime dispatcher's i18n domain relays an undeclared 5xx's text unless it looks like a leak: answered — not blocking, and it needs its own card, not an Acceptance note.** The dispatcher's thrown exit (`dispatcher-plugin.ts:689-797`) keeps an UNDECLARED 5xx legible unless `looksLikeInternalErrorLeak` fires; that tiering is a standing ruling (#5667, kept by the 2026-08-27 option D ruling) and the dispatcher is outside this card's surface, so it is not this PR's to change. But its reach is wider than "a divergence": by read-only inference the dispatcher is the LIVE door for the three exact i18n paths in a standard `os serve` boot. The dispatcher plugin mounts `${prefix}/i18n/locales`, `/translations/:locale`, `/labels/:object/:locale` inside `start()` (`dispatcher-plugin.ts:1480-1503`, unconditional once `http.server` resolves); `I18nServicePlugin` mounts the same three paths at `kernel:ready` (`i18n-service-plugin.ts:104-108`); the kernel fires `kernel:ready` in Phase 3, after every `start()` (`core/src/kernel.ts:596`); `plugin-hono-server`'s adapter pushes a second registration without dedupe (`adapter.ts:968-971`) and resolves by first-registration-wins (`hono-plugin.ts:246`); and ADR-0076 OQ#9's audit (#2462) already records that "in a standard boot ... the dispatcher bridge owns ... i18n". On that reading the three plugin arms this PR converts are shadowed in a standard boot, and the live door relays an undeclared throw's text whenever it does not read like SQL — `looksLikeInternalErrorLeak` covers dialect phrasings only, so a filesystem `EACCES ... open /srv/...` or `connect ECONNREFUSED host:port` passes it. The two dispatcher-only spellings (`/translations?locale=`, `/labels/:object?locale=`) are served by the dispatcher in every boot regardless. This is unmeasured on a real boot (read-only review; AGENTS.md says who serves a path is answered by booting the composition), so the card's first step is that measurement; its subject is Route ownership §1 (two owners of one path, one of them dead) plus the question for triage whether the i18n family's live door must withhold an undeclared 5xx's text the way this PR makes the plugin door do. Nothing here changes the correctness of the plugin-door conversion.

The prescription offered two shapes (the literal, or `resolveThrownHttpError(err).code`); the dev took the first and measured why — see ①2. The pins asked for are present: on both public token routes (`/:token/resolve`, `/:token/messages`) a throw with `code: '42P01'` and no status answers `500`, `error.code === 'INTERNAL'`, `BaseResponseSchema` parses the body, and `42P01` is nowhere in it. The five routes share one `mountFamilyRoute` catch, so the literal covers the three authenticated routes by construction. The record's corollary is pinned too: a caught `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` with no status costs one `[5xx]` `error` line with its stack and `console.warn` is never called. Negative control reported: restoring the pass-through turned 3 of 19 red with `expected '42P01' to be 'INTERNAL'`.

2. **The literal `'INTERNAL'`, against the dispatcher twin — right, and the spelling difference predates this PR; verified on `origin/main`.** `errorFromThrown` (`http-dispatcher.ts:1138-1175`) takes `error.code` from `resolveThrownHttpError(err, 500).code`, which is `registered ?? standardErrorCodeForHttpStatus(500)`, and `standardErrorCodeForHttpStatus(500)` is `INTERNAL_ERROR` (`spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts:192`). The twin's own pin, `runtime/src/domains/share-links-enforcement-context.test.ts:672-681`, drives a plain `new Error(...)` and asserts `INTERNAL_ERROR`, with a comment saying so against `INTERNAL`; the plugin door's own pin, `plugin-sharing/src/share-link-envelope.conformance.test.ts:343-349`, drives `throw new Error('boom')` through `createLink` and asserts `500 INTERNAL` — and at the merge base this door answered `err?.code ?? 'INTERNAL'`, which is `INTERNAL` for a plain Error. So the two mounts already disagreed on the plain-Error spelling before this PR, both spellings are catalogued (`INTERNAL` is an `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` member), and neither names a backend. Taking the resolver's code here would have (a) changed this door's plain-Error wire from `INTERNAL` to `INTERNAL_ERROR` against the standing conformance pin — a wire change outside this card — and (b) kept a registered no-status `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` / `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` on the wire and sent the fault through `logServerFault`'s capability-absence `warn` (no stack; and un-keyed, since the door passes no `request`), the corollary the record named. The literal closes both.
